title.zh: 卷九十四 晉書20: 列傳九 萇從簡 潘環 方太 何建 張廷蘊 郭延魯 郭金海 劉處讓 李瓊 高漢筠 孫彥韜 王傅拯 祕瓊 李彥珣
title.en: Volume 94 Book of Later Jin 20: Biographies 9 - Chang Congjian, Pan Huan, Fang Tai, He Jian, Zhang Tingyun, Guo Yanlu, Guo Jinhai, Liu Churang, Li Qiong, Gao Hanyun, Sun Yantao, Wang Fuzheng, Mi Qiong, Li Yanxun
title.raw: 卷九十四 晉書20: 列傳九 萇從簡 潘環 方太 何建 張廷蘊 郭延魯 郭金海 劉處讓 李瓊 高漢筠 孫彥韜 王傅拯 祕瓊 李彥珣 Volume 94 Book of Later Jin 20: Biographies 9 - Chang Congjian, Pan Huan, Fang Tai, He Jian, Zhang Tingyun, Guo Yanlu, Guo Jinhai, Liu Churang, Li Qiong, Gao Hanyun, Sun Yantao, Wang Fuzheng, Mi Qiong, Li Yanxun

sentences.zh: 萇從簡，陳州人也。

translations.literal: Chang Congjian was a native of Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Congjian was from Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 世以屠羊為業，力敵數人，善用槊。

translations.literal: For generations his family took butchering sheep as their trade; his strength could match several men, and he was skilled at using the spear.
translations.idiomatic: His family had butchered sheep for generations. He could match several men in strength and wielded the spear expertly.

sentences.zh: 初事後唐莊宗為小校，每遇攻城，召人為梯頭，從簡多應募焉，莊宗為其勇，擢領帳前親衛兼步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He first served Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong as a junior officer; whenever they besieged a city they called for men to lead the ladder assault, and Congjian often volunteered; Zhuangzong valued his courage and promoted him to command the personal guard before the throne together with commander of all foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Zhuangzong of Later Tang as a junior officer. In every siege the army called for ladder-team leaders, and Congjian often volunteered. Zhuangzong prized his courage and made him commander of the throne-guard escort and of all foot troops.

sentences.zh: 一日，莊宗領大軍與梁軍對陣，登高丘而坐，敵人有執大幟揚其武者，莊宗指之謂左右曰：「猛士也。

translations.literal: One day Zhuangzong led a great army to face the Liang army in battle array; he sat on a high mound, and among the enemy was one who held a great banner displaying his martial prowess; Zhuangzong pointed at him and said to those beside him: "A fierce warrior.
translations.idiomatic: One day Zhuangzong drew up his main force against Liang and sat on a high knoll. An enemy soldier was flourishing a great banner to show off his prowess. Zhuangzong pointed him out and told his attendants, "There's a fierce warrior.

sentences.zh: 」從簡曰：「臣為大王取之。

translations.literal: " Congjian said: "Your servant will take him for Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: " Congjian said, "I will fetch him for you, Great King."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗慮其不捷，不許。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong worried he might not succeed and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong feared he would fail and refused.

sentences.zh: 從簡退，乃潛領十數騎挺身而入，奪幟以歸，萬眾鼓噪，莊宗壯之，錫賚甚厚。

translations.literal: Congjian withdrew, then secretly led a dozen horsemen, charged in bodily, seized the banner and returned; the whole host cheered; Zhuangzong admired his feat and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian withdrew, then slipped away with a dozen horsemen, charged in alone, seized the banner, and rode back. The army roared approval. Zhuangzong was thrilled and heaped rewards on him.

sentences.zh: 又嘗中箭而鏃入於骨，使醫工出之，以刃鑿骨，恐其痛也，良久未能搖動。

translations.literal: On another occasion he was struck by an arrow and the arrowhead lodged in bone; he had a medical craftsman extract it, chiseling the bone with a blade; fearing his pain, for a long time they could not work it loose.
translations.idiomatic: He was once struck by an arrow whose head lodged in the bone. A surgeon was told to extract it by chiseling the bone with a blade. Fearing his pain, the man hesitated a long time and could not get it moving.

sentences.zh: 從簡嗔目謂曰：「何不沈鑿？

translations.literal: Congjian glared and said: "Why not chisel in deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Congjian glared and said, "Why not chisel hard?

sentences.zh: 」洎出之，左右無不惻然，從簡顏色自若，其勇壯皆此類也。

translations.literal: " When it came out, none on left or right were not moved to pity, yet Congjian's expression was as calm as ever; his courage and sturdiness were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " When the head came out, everyone nearby winced in sympathy, but Congjian's face stayed calm. His bravery was always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 從簡所為多不法，莊宗以其戰鬥多捷，常屈法赦之。

translations.literal: Much of what Congjian did was unlawful; Zhuangzong because his battles were often victorious, regularly bent the law and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian broke the law often. Zhuangzong bent the rules and pardoned him because he won so many battles.

sentences.zh: 賜姓，名曰紹瓊。

translations.literal: He was granted the imperial surname and given the name Shaojiong.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the imperial surname and given the name Shaojiong.

sentences.zh: 後加竭誠匡國功臣，累官至金紫光祿大夫、檢校太保、景州刺史，歷洺州團練使。

translations.literal: Later he was given the title Meritorious Subject of Utmost Loyalty Who Upholds the State; by successive promotions he reached Grand Master of Splendid Honor with Golden Seal, Grand Guardian by inspection, prefect of Jingzhou, and served as regimental commissioner of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Meritorious Subject of Utmost Loyalty Who Upholds the State and rose through Grand Master of Splendid Honor with Golden Seal, Grand Guardian by inspection, prefect of Jing, and regimental commissioner of Mo.

sentences.zh: 及梁平，典蔡州。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified, he was put in charge of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang fell, he governed Cai.

sentences.zh: 同光四年，授許州節度使，會莊宗晏駕，未及赴鎮而止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang he was appointed military governor of Xuzhou; when Zhuangzong died suddenly, he had not yet reached his post and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 4 he was made military governor of Xu, but Zhuangzong died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 明宗登極，例復本姓，歷麟、汝、汾、金四州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, by precedent he restored his original surname and served in succession as prefect of Lin, Ru, Fen, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Congjian recovered his original surname and served as prefect of Lin, Ru, Fen, and Jin in turn.

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》云：明宗尤惡貪貨，面戒汝州刺史萇從簡，為其貪暴。）〉

translations.literal: (Beimeng Suoyan says: Mingzong especially hated greed for goods and in person warned Congjian, prefect of Ru, for his greedy violence.)
translations.idiomatic: (Beimeng Suoyan says: Mingzong especially hated greed and personally warned Xu prefect Chang Congjian for his rapacity.)

sentences.zh: 應順初，舉軍伐鳳翔，從簡亦預其行，會軍變，乃東還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun the army marched to attack Fengxiang; Congjian took part in the campaign; when the army mutinied, they returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingshun the army marched on Fengxiang. Congjian went along, but when the troops mutinied the force turned back east.

sentences.zh: 道遇張廷蘊，為廷蘊所執，送於末帝。

translations.literal: On the road he met Zhang Tingyun, was seized by Tingyun, and sent to the Last Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he met Zhang Tingyun, who seized him and sent him to the Last Emperor.

sentences.zh: 末帝數之曰：「人皆歸我，爾何背我而去也？

translations.literal: The Last Emperor rebuked him, saying: "Everyone else has come over to me—why did you turn your back and leave?
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor scolded him: "Everyone has come to me. Why did you abandon me?

sentences.zh: 」從簡曰：「事主不敢二心，今日死生惟命。

translations.literal: " Congjian said: "In serving my lord I dare not have two hearts; today life or death are yours to command."
translations.idiomatic: " Congjian said, "I serve my lord with undivided loyalty. My life or death is yours to decide."

sentences.zh: 」末帝釋之。

translations.literal: " The Last Emperor released him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Last Emperor let him go.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年，授潁州團練使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he was appointed regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 2 he was made regimental commissioner of Ying.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉義，末帝將議親征，詔赴闕，充副招討使，隨駕至孟津，除河陽節度使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause, the Last Emperor was about to discuss a personal campaign and summoned him to court as deputy pacification commissioner; he followed the imperial carriage to Mengjin and was made military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose in revolt, the Last Emperor planned to campaign in person and summoned Congjian to court as deputy pacification commissioner. He accompanied the emperor to Mengjin and was made military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 及趙延壽軍敗，斷浮橋歸洛，留從簡守河陽。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yanshou's army was defeated, the floating bridge was cut and they returned to Luoyang; Congjian was left to hold Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yanshou's army was beaten, the floating bridge was cut and the force withdrew to Luoyang, leaving Congjian to hold Heyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖自北而至，從簡察軍情離散，遂渡河迎謁高祖。

translations.literal: When Gaozu came from the north, Congjian saw that military morale had scattered and crossed the river to meet and pay homage to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu arrived from the north. Seeing the army disintegrating, Congjian crossed the river to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 天福元年十二月，授許州節度使，改賜推忠佐運保國功臣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu he was appointed military governor of Xuzhou and granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Supports Loyalty and Aids Fortune in Protecting the State.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 1, month 12, he was made military governor of Xu and granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Supports Loyalty and Aids Fortune in Protecting the State.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，移鎮徐州。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year he was transferred to govern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, autumn, he was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，進封開國公，食邑至一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the status of Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of an independent office, Grand Preceptor by inspection, advanced to Duke Who Opens the State, with a fief reaching one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Grand Master of the Palace with independent office, Grand Preceptor by inspection, Duke Who Opens the State, with a fief of 1,500 households.

sentences.zh: 受代歸闕，授左金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When relieved and returned to court, he was appointed general-in-chief of the Left Golden Spear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Relieved of command, he returned to court and was made general-in-chief of the Left Golden Spear Guard.

sentences.zh: 從簡性忌刻而多疑，歷州鎮凡十餘，所在豎棘於公署，才通人行，左右稍違忤，即加鞭笞，或至殺害，其意不可測，吏人皆側行。

translations.literal: Congjian was jealous and suspicious by nature; over more than ten prefectures and garrisons he set thorn hedges in the government offices barely wide enough for a man to pass; if attendants on either side slightly offended him he would add flogging, sometimes even killing; his intent could not be fathomed, and clerks and subordinates all walked sideways.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was jealous and suspicious. In more than ten prefectures and garrisons he planted thorn hedges in government offices barely wide enough to pass. The slightest offense from an attendant brought a flogging, sometimes death. No one could guess his mood; staff walked sideways.

sentences.zh: 其煩苛暴虐，為武臣之最。

translations.literal: His vexatious harshness and cruelty were the worst among military men.
translations.idiomatic: Among military governors his petty cruelty was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，隨駕幸鄴都，遇疾請告，尋卒於鄉里，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he followed the imperial carriage to the northern capital; he fell ill and asked leave; soon he died in his home district at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, autumn, he accompanied the emperor to the northern capital, fell ill, asked leave, and soon died at home at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 潘環，字楚奇，洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Pan Huan, style Chuji, was a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Huan, courtesy name Chuji, was from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父景厚，以環貴，授左監門上將軍致仕。

translations.literal: His father Jinghou, because of Huan's eminence, was given Left Gate Guard general-in-chief and retired.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinghou, owing to Huan's rank, was made Left Gate Guard general-in-chief and retired.

sentences.zh: 環少以負販為業，始事梁邢州節度使閻寶，為帳中親校。

translations.literal: Huan in youth took peddling as his trade; he first served Yan Bao, military governor of Xingzhou under Liang, as a personal attendant in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Huan peddled for a living. He first served Liang's Xingzhou military governor Yan Bao as a personal attendant in headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗定魏博，移兵攻邢，寶遣環間道馳奏於梁，梁末帝用為左堅銳夾馬都虞候，累遷左雄威指揮使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Weibo and moved troops to attack Xing, Bao sent Huan by a secret route to report urgently to Liang; the Last Emperor of Liang used him as commander of the Left Firm Sharp Horse-Flanking Detachment and repeatedly promoted him to commander of the Left Majestic Might.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took Weibo and marched on Xing, Bao sent Huan by a secret route to urge Liang. The Last Emperor of Liang made him commander of the Left Firm Sharp Horse-Flanking Detachment and later commander of the Left Majestic Might.

sentences.zh: 時梁人與莊宗對壘於河上，環每預戰，先登陷敵，金瘡遍體。

translations.literal: At that time Liang and Zhuangzong faced each other on the river; Huan fought in every battle, charging first and breaking the enemy; wounds from metal weapons covered his body.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Zhuangzong faced off on the Yellow River. Huan fought in every clash, leading the charge; metal wounds covered his body.

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》云：潘環常中流矢於面，骨銜其鏃，故負重傷。

translations.literal: (Yutang Xianhua says: Pan Huan was once struck in the face by a flying arrow; the bone gripped the arrowhead, hence the heavy wound.
translations.idiomatic: (Yutang Xianhua says: Pan Huan once took an arrow in the face; the bone gripped the head, leaving a grave wound.

sentences.zh: 醫療至經年，其鏃自出，其瘡成漏，終身不痊。）〉

translations.literal: Medical treatment lasted nearly a year; the arrowhead came out on its own; the wound became a fistula and never healed for life.)
translations.idiomatic: Treatment took nearly a year before the head worked free. The wound became a fistula and never fully healed.)

sentences.zh: 莊宗知其名，及平梁，命典禁軍。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong knew his name, and when Liang was pacified appointed him to command the forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong knew his name. When Liang fell, he put him in charge of the forbidden army.

sentences.zh: 同光中，從明宗北禦契丹，鄴軍之亂，從明宗入洛。

translations.literal: In Tongguang he followed Mingzong north to resist the Khitan; in the mutiny of the Ye army he followed Mingzong into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tongguang he followed Mingzong north against the Khitan. In the Ye mutiny he followed Mingzong into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 天成初，授棣州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Di.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he was made prefect of Di.

sentences.zh: 會定州王都反，朝廷攻之，以環為行營右廂步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled and the court attacked him, Huan was made commander of the right wing foot army of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding's Wang Du rebelled, Huan was made commander of the campaign headquarters' right-wing foot army.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改易州刺史、北面沿邊都部署，後移刺慶州。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was changed to prefect of Yi and frontier deployment commander on the north, later transferred to govern Qing.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell he became Yi prefect and northern frontier deployment commander, then military governor of Qing.

sentences.zh: 受代歸闕，明宗召對，顧侍臣曰：「此人勇敢，少能偕者。

translations.literal: When relieved and returned to court, Mingzong summoned him for audience and told his attendants: "This man is brave; few can match him.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, Mingzong received him and told his ministers, "This man is brave. Few can equal him.

sentences.zh: 」尋除宿州團練使。

translations.literal: " Soon he was made regimental commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon made regimental commissioner of Su.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，移耀州。

translations.literal: In Qingtai he was transferred to Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qingtai he was moved to Yao.

sentences.zh: 天福中，預平範延光，授齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: In Tianfu he took part in pacifying Fan Yanguang and was appointed defender of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu he helped crush Fan Yanguang and was made defender of Qi.

sentences.zh: 四年，升金州為節鎮，以環為節度使，久之，入為左神武統軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jin prefecture was elevated to a garrison command; Huan was made its military governor; after a long time he entered court as commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Jin was elevated to a military governorship and Huan was made its governor. Later he entered court as commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 開運初，契丹入寇，王師北征，以環為北面行營步軍左廂排陣使，預破契丹於陽城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun the Khitan invaded; the royal army marched north; Huan was made array marshal of the left wing foot army of the northern campaign headquarters and took part in defeating the Khitan at Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun the Khitan invaded. Huan was made left-wing foot array marshal of the northern campaign and helped rout them at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 軍回，授澶州節度使，累官至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed military governor of Cao and rose by stages to Grand Preceptor by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made military governor of Cao and rose to Grand Preceptor by inspection.

sentences.zh: 三年，罷鎮歸闕，俄受詔洛京巡檢。

translations.literal: In the third year he left his garrison and returned to court; soon he received orders as Luoyang patrol inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he left his post and returned to court, then was ordered to patrol Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，戎王犯闕，偽署劉晞為西京留守，環乞罷巡警，閑居洛陽。

translations.literal: That winter the barbarian king breached the capital; Liu Xi was falsely appointed western capital regent; Huan begged to be relieved of patrol duty and lived idle in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Khitan took the capital. Liu Xi was installed as western capital regent. Huan asked off patrol duty and lived quietly in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遇河陽軍亂，晞出奔，未幾，蕃將高牟翰以兵援晞入於洛，慮環有變，乃害之，盡取其家財。

translations.literal: When Heyang troops mutinied, Xi fled; before long the barbarian general Gao Mouhan brought troops to support Xi into Luoyang; fearing Huan might change sides, they killed him and took all his family wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang mutinied and Xi fled. Soon the Khitan general Gao Mouhan entered Luoyang to support Xi. Fearing Huan might turn on them, they killed him and seized his family wealth.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云：晞疑環構其眾逐己，使牟翰殺之。）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian says: Xi suspected Huan had incited his men to drive him out and had Mouhan kill him.)
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian says: Xi suspected Huan had stirred his troops to expel him and had Mouhan kill him.)

sentences.zh: 漢高祖至京，贈太尉。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Han reached the capital, Huan was posthumously given Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Han reached the capital, Huan was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 環歷六部兩鎮，所至以聚斂為務。

translations.literal: Huan served in six ministries and two garrisons; wherever he went he made extortion his business.
translations.idiomatic: Huan held six prefectures and two military governorships and extorted wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 在宿州時，有牙將因微過見怒，環紿言笞之，牙校因托一尼嘗熟於環者，獻白金兩鋌。

translations.literal: While at Suzhou a junior officer angered him over a trifle; Huan pretended to say he would flog him; the officer's deputy therefore asked a nun who was on familiar terms with Huan to present two ingots of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: At Su a junior officer angered him over a small matter. Huan pretended he would flog him. The man's deputy asked a nun who knew Huan well to offer two ingots of white gold.

sentences.zh: 尼詣環白牙校餉𨫼腳兩枚，求免其責，環曰：「𨫼本幾腳？

translations.literal: The nun told Huan that the deputy was offering two ingots of foot-money and begged to spare his punishment; Huan said: "How many feet does foot-money come to?
translations.idiomatic: The nun said the deputy was offering two ingots of "foot-money" and begged mercy. Huan asked, "How many feet is foot-money?

sentences.zh: 」尼曰：「三腳。

translations.literal: " The nun said: "Three feet."
translations.idiomatic: " The nun said, "Three feet."

sentences.zh: 」環復曰：「今兩腳能成𨫼乎？

translations.literal: " Huan again said: "Can two feet make foot-money?
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "Can two feet make foot-money?

sentences.zh: 」尼則以三數致之，當時號環為「潘𨫼腳」。

translations.literal: " The nun then brought the full three; at the time they called Huan "Pan Foot-Money."
translations.idiomatic: " She brought three. People nicknamed him "Pan Foot-Money."

sentences.zh: 方太，字伯宗，青州千乘人也。

translations.literal: Fang Tai, style Bozong, was a native of Qiancheng in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Tai, courtesy name Bozong, was from Qiancheng in Qing.

sentences.zh: 少隸本軍為小校，嘗戍登州，劫海客，事泄，刺史淳於晏匿之，遇赦免。

translations.literal: In youth he was attached to his home army as a junior officer; he once garrisoned Dengzhou and robbed seagoing merchants; when the matter leaked out, Prefect Chunyu Yan hid him; he was spared by an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served his home army as a junior officer. Garrisoned at Deng, he robbed seagoing merchants. When exposed, Prefect Chunyu Yan sheltered him until an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 事定州節度使楊光遠，光遠領兵赴晉陽。

translations.literal: He served Dingzhou military governor Yang Guangyuan; Guangyuan led troops to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served Ding military governor Yang Guangyuan, who marched troops to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 本州軍亂，太與馬萬、盧順密等擒之，使太縛送至闕。

translations.literal: The home prefecture mutinied; Tai with Ma Wan, Lu Shunmi, and others seized him; they had Tai bind him and send him to court.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture mutinied. Tai with Ma Wan and Lu Shunmi seized Guangyuan and had Tai bind him for the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋從杜重威破張從賓於汜水，以功除趙州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Du Chongwei in defeating Zhang Congbin at Sishui and by merit was made prefect of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Du Chongwei in defeating Zhang Congbin at Sishui and was made Zhao prefect for his merit.

sentences.zh: 從楊光遠平範延光於鄴，移刺萊州，遷安州防禦使。

translations.literal: He followed Yang Guangyuan in pacifying Fan Yanguang at Ye, was transferred to govern Lai, and promoted to defender of An.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yang Guangyuan against Fan Yanguang at Ye, governed Lai, then became defender of An.

sentences.zh: 從少帝幸澶州，與契丹戰於戚城，中數創，改鳳州防禦使，行至中途，遷河陽留後，移邢州留後。

translations.literal: He followed the Young Emperor to Cao and fought the Khitan at Weicheng, took several wounds, was made defender of Feng, and on the road was made regent of Heyang and then regent of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Young Emperor to Cao, fought the Khitan at Weicheng, took several wounds, was made Feng defender, then Heyang regent en route, then Xing regent.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯闕，偽命遙領洋州節度使，充洛京巡檢，與前洺州團練使李瓊俱至鄭州，其屯駐兵士迫請太在城巡檢，以備外盜，號為「鄭王」。

translations.literal: When the Khitan breached the capital they falsely appointed him military governor of Yang in absentia and Luoyang patrol inspector; with former Mo regimental commissioner Li Qiong he reached Zhengzhou; the garrison troops forced Tai to patrol the city against outside bandits and called him "King of Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took the capital they named him absentee Yang military governor and Luoyang patrol inspector. He and former Mo regimental commissioner Li Qiong reached Zheng. The garrison forced him to patrol against bandits and called him "King of Zheng."

sentences.zh: 時有嵩山賊帥張遇，領眾萬餘，於僧眾得梁朝故嗣密王朱乙，遂推為天子，取嵩山神冠冕之服以衣之。

translations.literal: At the time the bandit chief Zhang Yu on Mount Song led more than ten thousand men; among the monks they obtained Zhu Yi, the late Liang's heir Prince of Secret Succession, and made him Son of Heaven, taking the divine crown and robes of Mount Song to clothe him.
translations.idiomatic: Song bandit chief Zhang Yu led ten thousand men. Among monks they found Zhu Yi, Liang's late heir Prince of Secret Succession, made him emperor, and dressed him in Mount Song ritual regalia.

sentences.zh: 張遇以其眾攻鄭州，太與李瓊擊之，賊眾敗走，瓊中流矢而死。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu led his host to attack Zhengzhou; Tai and Li Qiong struck them; the bandits were beaten and fled; Qiong died of a wound from a flying arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu attacked Zheng. Tai and Li Qiong repulsed him. The bandits fled; Qiong died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 太乃括率郡中財物以賞軍士，因誘之欲同西去，其眾不從，太乃潛奔於洛陽。

translations.literal: Tai then levied the prefecture's wealth to reward the soldiers and tried to lure them west; the host would not follow; Tai then slipped away to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tai levied prefectural wealth to reward the troops and tried to lure them west. They refused. He slipped away to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云：戍兵既失太，反譖太於契丹，雲脅我為亂。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian says: The garrison troops, having lost Tai, in turn slandered Tai to the Khitan, saying he had coerced them into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian says: Losing Tai, the garrison slandered him to the Khitan, claiming he had forced them into revolt.

sentences.zh: 太遣子師朗自訴於契丹，契丹殺之。）〉

translations.literal: Tai sent his son Shilang to plead to the Khitan; the Khitan killed him.)
translations.idiomatic: Tai sent his son Shilang to plead. The Khitan killed him.)

sentences.zh: 及劉晞南走許州，太殺晞牙校李暉，入河南府行留守事。

translations.literal: When Liu Xi fled south to Xuzhou, Tai killed Xi's junior officer Li Hui and entered Henan prefecture to act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xi fled south to Xu, Tai killed his officer Li Hui and entered Henan to act as regent.

sentences.zh: 既而嵩山賊帥張遇殺嗣密王，傳首於太，懸於洛市。

translations.literal: Soon the Song bandit chief Zhang Yu killed the Prince of Secret Succession and sent his head to Tai, who hung it in the Luoyang market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu killed the false emperor and sent his head to Tai, who displayed it in the Luoyang market.

sentences.zh: 又有伊闕賊帥自稱天子，領眾萬餘，將入洛城，集郊壇之上，太率兵數百人逆擊，破之，賊眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Another bandit chief at Yique called himself Son of Heaven and led more than ten thousand men about to enter Luoyang and gathered on the suburban altar; Tai led several hundred men to strike them, broke them, and the bandits dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Another Yique bandit styled himself emperor with ten thousand men and massed at the suburban altar to enter Luoyang. Tai led hundreds against them, routed them, and they scattered.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》引實錄《方太傳》云：劉禧走許田，復有潁陽妖巫，姓朱，號嗣密王，誓眾於洛南天壇，號萬餘人。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian Kaoyi citing the Veritable Records Fang Tai biography says: Liu Xi fled to Xutian; again a sorcerer of Yingyang surnamed Zhu called himself heir Prince of Secret Succession and swore an oath at the southern Luoyang altar with more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian Kaoyi, citing the Veritable Records biography of Fang Tai, says: Liu Xi fled toward Xu. A Yingyang sorcerer surnamed Zhu styled himself heir Prince of Secret Succession and mustered ten thousand at Luoyang's southern altar.

sentences.zh: 太帥部曲與朝士輩虛張旗幟，一舉而逐之，洛師遂安。）〉

translations.literal: Tai led his troops with court officials to raise banners falsely and in one stroke drove them off; the Luoyang army was then secure.)
translations.idiomatic: Tai led his men and courtiers with sham banners and drove them off in one stroke, securing Luoyang.)

sentences.zh: 河陽武行德遣使召太，詐言欲推之為帥，尋為行德所害。

translations.literal: Wu Xingde of Heyang sent a messenger summoning Tai, falsely saying he wished to push him as commander, but soon Xingde killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang's Wu Xingde summoned Tai, pretending he would make him commander, then killed him.

sentences.zh: 何建，其先回鶻人也，代居雲、朔間。

translations.literal: He Jian—his ancestors were Uyghurs who for generations dwelt between Yun and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian was of Uyghur descent; his family had lived between Yun and Shuo for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖慶，父懷福，俱事後唐武皇為小校。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qing and father Huai Fu both served Later Tang's Martial Emperor as junior officers.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qing and father Huai Fu both served Later Tang's Martial Emperor as junior officers.

sentences.zh: 建少以謹厚隸於高祖帳下，以掌廄為役，及即位，累典禁軍，

translations.literal: Jian in youth, by his prudent steadiness, was attached to Gaozu's headquarters, serving in the stables; when Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly commanded the forbidden army,
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jian's steady character won him a place in Gaozu's stables. After Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly commanded the forbidden army,

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：重建初事晉祖為奉德馬軍都指揮使。）〉

translations.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi says: Early in rebuilding the state he served the Jin founder as commander of the Fengde Horse Army.)
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuguo Zhi says: Early on he served the Jin founder as commander of the Fengde Horse Army.)

sentences.zh: 遙領歡、睦二郡。

translations.literal: He held Huan and Mu prefectures in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: He held Huan and Mu in absentia.

sentences.zh: 天福中，自曹州刺史遷延州兵馬留後，尋正授旄鉞。

translations.literal: In Tianfu he moved from Cao prefect to regent of Yanzhou troops, soon receiving the full commission with banner and axe.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu he rose from Cao prefect to Yanzhou regent, then full military governor.

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：延州節度使丁審琪殘暴貪冒，蕃部苦之。

translations.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi says: Yanzhou military governor Ding Shenqi was brutal and greedy; the frontier tribes suffered.
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuguo Zhi says: Yan military governor Ding Shenqi was brutal and greedy; frontier tribes suffered.

sentences.zh: 重建以所部兵攻其城，審琪遁去，晉祖即以重建權節度兵馬留後，下車諭以威福，邊民安堵，就加彰武軍節度使。）〉

translations.literal: Jian rebuilt attacked his city with his troops; Shenqi fled; the Jin founder at once made Jian acting regent of Yanzhou troops, and on taking office he lectured on authority and favor so the frontier people were secure; he was then given Zhangwu Army military governor.)
translations.idiomatic: Jian attacked his city; Shenqi fled. The Jin founder made Jian acting Yan regent. On taking office he lectured on authority and favor; the frontier settled, and he was made Zhangwu military governor.)

sentences.zh: 數年之間，歷涇、鄧、貝、澶、孟五鎮節度使，

translations.literal: Within several years he served in succession as military governor of Jing, Deng, Bei, Cao, and Meng—five garrisons,
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he governed Jing, Deng, Bei, Cao, and Meng in succession,

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：皆以廉儉簡易稱。）〉

translations.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi says: All were praised for integrity, thrift, and simplicity.)
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuguo Zhi says: All were known for integrity, thrift, and simplicity.)

sentences.zh: 累官至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: By successive promotions he reached Grand Preceptor by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Preceptor by inspection.

sentences.zh: 開運三年，移鎮秦州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyun he was transferred to govern Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 3 he was transferred to Qin.

sentences.zh: 是冬，契丹入汴，其主遣人賫詔以賜建，建憤然謂將吏曰：「吾事石氏二主，累擁戎旃，人臣之榮，亦已極矣。

translations.literal: That winter the Khitan entered Bian, and their ruler sent someone bearing an edict to bestow on Jian; Jian said angrily to his officers: "I have served the two lords of the Shi clan and repeatedly held the battle-banner— the glory of a subject could not go further.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Khitan took Bian and sent an edict to Jian. He told his officers angrily, "I served both Shi emperors and held command banners many times—the honor of a subject could go no higher.

sentences.zh: 今日不能率兵赴難，豈可受制於契丹乎！

translations.literal: Today I cannot lead troops to the rescue—how can I be controlled by the Khitan!
translations.idiomatic: Today I cannot march to save the dynasty. How can I submit to the Khitan?

sentences.zh: 」即遣使賫表與其地送款於蜀，孟昶待之甚厚，偽加同平章事，依前秦州節度使。

translations.literal: " He at once sent an envoy bearing a memorial and his territory to offer allegiance to Shu; Meng Chang treated him very generously, falsely made him co-equal director of the Secretariat, and left him as before military governor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent envoys with a memorial and his territory to Shu. Meng Chang received him generously, made him co-equal director of the Secretariat in name, and left him Qin military governor.

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：時固鎮與鳳州未平，重建悉經略討平之。）〉

translations.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi says: At the time Guzhen and Fengzhou were not yet pacified; Jian rebuilt thoroughly planned and pacified them.)
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuguo Zhi says: Guzhen and Feng were not yet pacified; Jian campaigned and pacified them.)

sentences.zh: 歲餘，移閬州保寧軍節度使，

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to military governor of Langzhou, Baoning Army,
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made Baoning Army military governor of Lang,

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：昶大舉兵北伐，遣張虔釗出大散關，以重建為招討使，由隴州路以進師，無功而還。）〉

translations.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi says: Chang launched a great northern campaign and sent Zhang Qianzhao out through Dasanguan, making Jian rebuilt pacification commissioner to advance by the Longzhou route; they returned without success.)
translations.idiomatic: (Jiuguo Zhi says: Chang launched a northern campaign and sent Zhang Qianzhao through Dasanguan, with Jian as pacification commissioner advancing by the Long route; they returned without success.)

sentences.zh: 加偽官至中書令，後卒於蜀。

translations.literal: He was given false rank up to Director of the Secretariat and later died in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given false rank through Director of the Secretariat and later died in Shu.

sentences.zh: 張廷蘊，字德樞，開封襄邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Tingyun, style Deshu, was a native of Xiangyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyun, courtesy name Deshu, was from Xiangyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖立，贈驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Li was posthumously given General of the Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Li was posthumously made General of the Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 父及，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Ji was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Honor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Honor.

sentences.zh: 廷蘊少勇捷，始隸宣武軍為伍長，唐天復中，奔太原，武皇收於帳下為小校。

translations.literal: Tingyun in youth was brave and agile; he first served the Xuanwu Army as a squad leader; in Tianfu of Tang he fled to Taiyuan, and the Martial Emperor took him into headquarters as a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Tingyun was brave and quick. He joined the Xuanwu Army as squad leader, fled to Taiyuan in Tang Tianfu, and the Martial Emperor took him as a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗救上黨，戰柏鄉，攻薊門，下邢、魏，皆從之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong rescued Shangdang he fought at Bai Township, attacked Jimen, and took Xing and Wei—all with Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong rescuing Shangdang, fighting at Bai Township, taking Jimen, Xing, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 後戰於莘縣及胡柳陂，繼為流矢所中，金瘡之痕，盈於面首。

translations.literal: Later he fought at Shen County and Huliupo and in succession was struck by flying arrows; marks from metal wounds covered his face and head.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Shen County and Huliupo he took arrow after arrow; metal wounds covered his face and head.

sentences.zh: 莊宗寵之，統御營黃甲軍，常在左右，累加檢校兵部尚書、帳前步軍都虞候，充諸軍濠寨使。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong favored him; he commanded the Imperial Camp Yellow Armor Army and was always at his side; he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of War by inspection, commander of foot troops before the throne, and superintendent of moats and stockades for all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong favored him, put him in charge of the Yellow Armor Army, and kept him close. He rose to Minister of War by inspection, throne-guard foot commander, and superintendent of siege works for all armies.

sentences.zh: 同光初，從明宗收汶陽，加檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博三城巡檢使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he followed Mingzong in recovering Wenyang, was given Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat by inspection, and made inspector of the three cities of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he followed Mingzong to recover Wenyang, was made Vice Director of the Right by inspection, and inspector of Weibo's three cities.

sentences.zh: 時皇后劉氏在鄴，每縱其下擾人，廷蘊多斬之，聞者壯焉。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Liu was at Ye and often let her followers harass the people; Tingyun often beheaded them, and those who heard were impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu was at Ye and let her men harass people. Tingyun often executed them, to general approval.

sentences.zh: 梁平，承詔入覲，改帳前都指揮使兼左右羽林都虞候。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified he received orders to attend court and was changed to commander before the throne together with commander of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell he attended court and became commander before the throne and of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers.

sentences.zh: 會李繼韜故將楊立叛，詔遣明宗為招討使，元行欽為都部署，廷蘊為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the former officer of Li Jirao, Yang Li, rebelled, an edict sent Mingzong as pacification commissioner, Yuan Xingqin as campaign commander, and Tingyun as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jirao's officer Yang Li rebelled, Mingzong was made pacification commissioner, Yuan Xingqin campaign commander, and Tingyun vanguard.

sentences.zh: 軍至上黨，日已暝矣，憩軍方定，廷蘊首率勁兵百餘輩，逾洫坎城而上，守陴者不能禦，尋斬關延諸軍入焉。

translations.literal: The army reached Shangdang; the day had already darkened and the army had just settled when Tingyun first led a hundred-odd picked troops, crossed the moat and climbed the wall; the defenders on the parapet could not resist, and soon they cut the gate and led the armies in.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Shangdang at dusk. Tingyun led a hundred picked men over the moat onto the wall, defenders could not stop them, and he opened the gate for the main force.

sentences.zh: 明宗、行欽達明而始至，其城已下，明宗甚慊之。

translations.literal: Mingzong and Xingqin reached at dawn and the city was already taken; Mingzong was very displeased with this.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong and Xingqin arrived at dawn to find the city already taken. Mingzong was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 軍還，改左右羽林都指揮使，加檢校司空，行申州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was changed to commander of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers, given Minister of Works by inspection, and acted as prefect of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became commander of the Forest of Feathers, Minister of Works by inspection, and acting Shen prefect.

sentences.zh: 同光末，從皇子魏王繼岌伐蜀，授行營中軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang he followed the prince of Wei, Jiji, in the Shu campaign and was appointed commander of the central army of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tongguang he followed Prince of Wei Jiji against Shu as central army commander of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，明宗嗣位，遷懷州刺史，賜竭忠建策興復功臣，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified and Mingzong succeeded, he was moved to Huai prefect and given the title Meritorious Subject of Utmost Loyalty Who Devises Strategy for Restoration, and Grand Master of Ceremonies by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell and Mingzong succeeded, he became Huai prefect and Meritorious Subject of Utmost Loyalty Who Devises Strategy for Restoration, Grand Master of Ceremonies by inspection.

sentences.zh: 旋移金州防禦使，加檢校太保，繼授潁州團練使、沿淮招安使。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to defender of Jin, given Grand Guardian by inspection, and in succession regimental commissioner of Ying and pacification commissioner along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Jin defender, Grand Guardian by inspection, then Ying regimental commissioner and Huai pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 應順中，轉隴州防禦使。

translations.literal: In Yingshun he was transferred to defender of Long.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yingshun he was moved to Long defender.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，進封清河郡公。

translations.literal: In Qingtai he was advanced to Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qingtai he was made Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，入為右龍武統軍，遷絳州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he entered court as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army and was moved to defender of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he entered as Right Dragon Martial commander, then Jiang defender.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，領左軍衛上將軍，加特進。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded he led the Left Army Guard general-in-chief and was given special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded he became Left Army Guard general-in-chief with special advancement.

sentences.zh: 開運三年冬，以老病求歸於宋城，明年卒於家，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Kaiyun, because of old age and illness he asked to return to Songcheng; the next year he died at home at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 3, winter, he asked leave to return to Songcheng and died at home the next year at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 廷蘊所識不過數字，而性重文士。

translations.literal: Tingyun knew no more than a few characters, yet by nature he valued literary men.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun knew barely a few characters yet valued scholars.

sentences.zh: 下汶陽日，首獲鄆帥戴思遠判官趙鳳，訊之曰：「爾狀貌必儒人也，勿隱其情。

translations.literal: On the day he took Wenyang he first captured Yan military commander Dai Siyuan's judge Zhao Feng and questioned him: "Your appearance must be that of a Confucian—do not hide the facts."
translations.idiomatic: Taking Wenyang he captured Yan commander Dai Siyuan's aide Zhao Feng and said, "You look like a scholar—don't hide it."

sentences.zh: 」鳳具言之，尋引薦於明宗，明宗令送赴行臺，尋除鳳翰林學士。

translations.literal: " Feng stated it fully; Tingyun soon recommended him to Mingzong, and Mingzong had him sent to the field headquarters and soon made Feng a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Feng told all. Tingyun recommended him to Mingzong, who sent him to headquarters and soon made him Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 及鳳入相，頗與廷蘊相洽，數言於近臣安重誨，重誨亦以廷蘊苦戰出於諸將之右，力保薦之。

translations.literal: When Feng entered the chancellorship he was quite close with Tingyun and often spoke to the close minister An Chonghui; Chonghui also because Tingyun's bitter fighting stood above the other generals strongly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng became chancellor he stayed close to Tingyun and spoke often to An Chonghui, who also backed him because his fighting surpassed other generals.

sentences.zh: 明宗以廷蘊取潞之日，不能讓功於己，故恒蓄宿忿，至使廷蘊位竟不至方鎮，亦命矣夫！

translations.literal: Mingzong because on the day Tingyun took Lu he could not yield merit to himself always harbored an old grudge, so that Tingyun's rank in the end never reached a frontier command—it was fate!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong resented that Tingyun took Lu without yielding credit, so he never gave him a frontier post—such was fate.

sentences.zh: 廷蘊歷七郡，家無餘積，年老耋期，終於牖下，良可嘉也。

translations.literal: Tingyun served seven prefectures yet his family had no surplus wealth; in old age he ended beneath his window—truly admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He held seven posts yet left no surplus wealth and died at home in old age—a life to admire.

sentences.zh: 長子光被，歷通事舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guangbei served through Grand Secretariat courier.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guangbei rose to Grand Secretariat courier.

sentences.zh: 郭金海，本突厥之族。

translations.literal: Guo Jinhai was originally of the Turkic tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jinhai was of Turkic stock.

sentences.zh: 少侍昭義節度使李嗣昭，常從征伐。

translations.literal: In youth he attended Zhaoyi military governor Li Sizhao and often followed on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served Zhaoyi military governor Li Sizhao on campaign.

sentences.zh: 金海好酒，所為不法，自潞州過山東，入邢洺界為劫盜，嗣昭雖知之，然惜其拳勇，每優容之。

translations.literal: Jinhai loved wine and acted unlawfully; passing from Luzhou through Shandong into Xing and Mo territory he became a robber-bandit; Sizhao though he knew it yet cherished his fist-bravery and each time treated him indulgently.
translations.idiomatic: Jinhai drank and broke the law. Leaving Luzhou he robbed in Xing and Mo. Sizhao knew but indulged him for his strength.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，累職至昭義親騎指揮使。

translations.literal: In Tianyou he rose by stages to commander of Zhaoyi's personal horse guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianyou he rose to commander of Zhaoyi's personal horse guard.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，遷本道馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he was moved to commander of this circuit's horse army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 2 he became this circuit's horse army commander.

sentences.zh: 天成初，入為捧聖指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he entered court as commander of the Supporting Sage Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he entered as Supporting Sage commander.

sentences.zh: 長興三年，改護聖都虞候。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changxing he was changed to commander of the Protecting Sage.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 3 he became Protecting Sage commander.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，從王師討範延光於魏州，以功轉本軍都指揮使，領黃州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he followed the royal army in attacking Fan Yanguang at Weizhou and by merit was transferred to commander of this army and prefect of Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 2 he helped attack Fan Yanguang at Wei and became army commander and Huang prefect.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸鄴，宣金海領部兵巡檢東京。

translations.literal: When Gaozu visited Ye he announced Jinhai would lead his troops to patrol the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu visited Ye he had Jinhai patrol the eastern capital with his troops.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，安從進謀犯闕，金海為襄州道行營先鋒都指揮使，與李建崇等同於唐州湖陽遇從進軍萬餘人，金海以一旅之眾突擊，大敗之，策勛授檢校太保、商州刺史，俄移慶州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year An Congjin plotted to assault the capital; Jinhai was vanguard commander of the Xiangzhou route campaign headquarters; with Li Jianchong and others at Huyang in Tang prefecture they met Congjin's army of more than ten thousand; Jinhai with one detachment charged and greatly defeated them; for merit he was given Grand Guardian by inspection and Shang prefect, soon moved to Qing.
translations.idiomatic: That November An Congjin rebelled. Jinhai was Xiang-route vanguard. At Huyang in Tang he met Congjin's ten thousand with one detachment, routed them, and was made Grand Guardian by inspection and Shang prefect, then Qing.

sentences.zh: 秩滿歸闕，途中遇疾而卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to court; on the road he met illness and died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled when his term ended, he fell ill on the road and died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: （《洛陽縉紳舊聞記》：從進與金海相遇於花山。

translations.literal: (Old Accounts of Luoyang Gentry says: Congjin and Jinhai met at Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: (Old Accounts of Luoyang Gentry says: Congjin and Jinhai met at Huashan.

sentences.zh: 金海蕃將，善用槍，時罕與敵，拳勇過人，喜戰鬥，欲立奇功。

translations.literal: Jinhai was a barbarian general skilled with the spear, at the time rarely matched, surpassing men in fist-bravery, loving battle, wishing to win singular merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jinhai, a frontier general, wielded the spear like few others, loved combat, and sought glory.

sentences.zh: 兩陣相去數里。

translations.literal: The two arrays were several li apart.
translations.idiomatic: The armies stood several li apart.

sentences.zh: 從進素管騎兵，金海久在麾下，從進亦待之素厚。

translations.literal: Congjin had long commanded horse troops; Jinhai had long been under him; Congjin also always treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin had long led cavalry and treated Jinhai generously.

sentences.zh: 乃躍馬引數百騎乘高，去金海陣數百步，厲聲呼「郭金海」。

translations.literal: He then spurred his horse and led several hundred horsemen to a height several hundred paces from Jinhai's array and shouted loudly "Guo Jinhai."
translations.idiomatic: He rode to a height several hundred paces off and shouted "Guo Jinhai!"

sentences.zh: 金海獨鞭馬出於陣數十步，免胄側身，高聲自稱曰「金海」。

translations.literal: Jinhai alone whipped his horse out several tens of paces from the array, removed his helmet and turned aside, and loudly called himself "Jinhai."
translations.idiomatic: Jinhai rode out alone, doffed his helmet, and shouted back "Jinhai!"

sentences.zh: 從進又前行數十步，勞之曰：「金海安否？

translations.literal: Congjin again advanced several tens of paces and comforted him: "Is Jinhai well?
translations.idiomatic: Congjin rode closer and called, "Are you well, Jinhai?

sentences.zh: 我素待爾厚，略不知恩，今日敢來共我相殺？

translations.literal: I always treated you thickly—you slightly know no gratitude; today you dare come to fight me to the death?
translations.idiomatic: I always treated you well. You repay me by coming to kill me?

sentences.zh: 」金海應聲答曰：「官家好看大王，負大王甚事，大王今日反？

translations.literal: " Jinhai answered at once: "Your Majesty look well to the Great King—the Great King has wronged you in nothing; why does the Great King rebel today?
translations.idiomatic: " Jinhai shouted back, "Look after the Prince! He never wronged you—why rebel?

sentences.zh: 金海舊事大王，乞與大王一箭地，大王回去，若不去，吃取金海槍。

translations.literal: Jinhai's old affair is with the Great King—beg one arrow's ground; the Great King go back; if you do not go, eat Jinhai's spear.
translations.idiomatic: I served the Prince. Give him room to withdraw—or taste my spear.

sentences.zh: 」言訖，援槍鞭馬，疾趨其陣。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking he seized his spear, whipped his horse, and swiftly returned to his array.
translations.idiomatic: " He wheeled back to his lines with spear raised.

sentences.zh: 從進懼，躍馬而進，師遂相接，大為金海、焦繼勛摧敗。

translations.literal: Congjin was afraid, spurred his horse forward, and the armies then joined battle and were greatly crushed by Jinhai and Jiao Jixun.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin charged; the armies clashed and Jinhai and Jiao Jixun routed them.

sentences.zh: 奏到，晉祖大喜，賞賜有差。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the Jin founder was greatly pleased and rewards were graded.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 從進自此喪氣，嬰城自固，王師為連城重塹以守之。

translations.literal: From this Congjin lost his spirit, held the city and fortified himself, and the royal army made linked cities and deep moats to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin lost heart, held the city, and the royal army besieged with linked trenches.

sentences.zh: 月餘，王師攻城，城上矢下如雨，王師被傷者眾。

translations.literal: After more than a month the royal army assaulted the city; arrows from the wall fell like rain and many of the royal army were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: After a month they assaulted the walls. Arrows fell like rain and many were wounded.

sentences.zh: 是日，金海為飛矢集身，扶傷歸營。

translations.literal: That day Jinhai was struck by flying arrows all over his body and was helped back wounded to camp.
translations.idiomatic: That day arrows covered Jinhai; he was helped back wounded.

sentences.zh: 明日，從進用計汙金海，欲使朝廷疑之。

translations.literal: The next day Congjin used a stratagem to slander Jinhai, wishing to make the court suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Congjin slandered him to sow court suspicion.

sentences.zh: 以金瓶貯酒，金合盛藥，以索懸之，城上呼「郭金海」。

translations.literal: He hung a golden bottle of wine and a golden box of medicine by a rope, called from the wall "Guo Jinhai,"
translations.idiomatic: He lowered a gold wine bottle and medicine box on ropes and called "Guo Jinhai!"

sentences.zh: 金海知之，力疾扶創而往。

translations.literal: Jinhai knew it and, forcing his illness, went supported by his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Jinhai knew and dragged himself there despite his wounds.

sentences.zh: 城上勞金海曰：「大王知爾中箭創甚，賜爾金瓶金合酒與風藥。

translations.literal: From the wall they comforted Jinhai: "The Great King knows you were heavily wounded by an arrow and bestows on you a golden bottle and golden box of wine and wind medicine."
translations.idiomatic: From the wall they said, "The Prince knows you are badly wounded and sends wine and medicine."

sentences.zh: 」金海目不知書，惟利是貪，取瓶與合歸營，且不聞於元戎。

translations.literal: Jinhai could not read and only coveted profit; he took the bottle and box back to camp and did not report to the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate and greedy, he took the gifts to camp without telling his commander.

sentences.zh: 元戎等疑之，乃馳驛奏。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief and others suspected him and hurried a memorial by post.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders suspected treason and reported by express.

sentences.zh: 晉祖以花山之功，不加罪。

translations.literal: The Jin founder because of the Huashan merit did not add guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu spared him for Huashan.

sentences.zh: 城下，就除金州團練，並其兵於他部。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was made on the spot regimental commissioner of Jin and his troops were merged into another unit.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was made Jin regimental commissioner and his troops were reassigned.

sentences.zh: 金海之任，居常悒悒不樂，至於捐館。）〉

translations.literal: Jinhai's appointment—he was always depressed and unhappy, until he died at his post.)
translations.idiomatic: He remained miserable in office until he died.)

sentences.zh: 劉處讓，字德謙，滄州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Churang, style Deqian, was a native of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Churang, courtesy name Deqian, was from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖信，累贈太子少保。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xin was repeatedly posthumously given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xin was posthumously Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父喻，累贈太子少師。

translations.literal: His father Yu was repeatedly posthumously given Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was posthumously Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明初，張萬進帥兗州，處讓事之，為親校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming under Liang, Zhang Wanjin commanded Yanzhou; Churang served him as a personal attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang Zhenming, Zhang Wanjin commanded Yan. Churang served him as personal attendant.

sentences.zh: 萬進據城叛，梁遣大將劉鄩討之。

translations.literal: Wanjin held the city in rebellion; Liang sent the great general Liu Yan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin rebelled and Liang sent Liu Yan against him.

sentences.zh: 時唐莊宗屯軍於麻口渡，萬進密遣處讓乞師於莊宗，莊宗未即應之，乃於軍門截耳曰：「主帥急難，使我告援，茍不得請，死亦何避。

translations.literal: At the time Tang's Zhuangzong encamped at Makou Ford; Wanjin secretly sent Churang to beg troops from Zhuangzong; Zhuangzong did not immediately respond; he then at the army gate cut off his ear and said: "The commander is in urgent peril and sent me to announce for aid; if I cannot obtain it, what is there to avoid in death?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong camped at Makou. Wanjin sent Churang to beg aid. Unanswered, Churang cut off his ear at the gate: "My commander is desperate. If you refuse, death is nothing.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗義之，將舉兵渡河，俄聞城陷乃止。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong considered it righteous and was about to lead troops across the river; soon he heard the city had fallen and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Moved, Zhuangzong prepared to cross—but the city fell and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 因以墨制授處讓行臺左驍衛將軍，俄改客省副使。

translations.literal: He therefore gave Churang by ink edict the post of Left Valiant Guard general of the field headquarters and soon changed him to deputy commissioner of the Reception Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He made Churang Left Valiant Guard general of the field headquarters, then Reception Bureau deputy.

sentences.zh: 梁平，加檢校兵部尚書，累將命稱旨。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified he was given Minister of War by inspection and repeatedly carried orders to satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell he was Minister of War by inspection and carried missions well.

sentences.zh: 天成初，轉檢校尚書右僕射，依前充職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat by inspection and continued in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he became Vice Director of the Right by inspection in the same role.

sentences.zh: 歲餘遷引進使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was moved to commissioner of introductions.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became commissioner of introductions.

sentences.zh: 長興三年，轉檢校司空、左威衛大將軍，其職如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changxing he was transferred to Minister of Works by inspection and Left Majestic Guard general-in-chief, his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 3 he was Minister of Works by inspection and Left Majestic Guard general-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，西川孟知祥跋扈，不通朝貢，朝廷方議懷柔，乃遣處讓為官告國信使，復命，轉檢校司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Meng Zhixiang of western Shu was overbearing and did not send court tribute; the court was discussing appeasement and sent Churang as credence envoy bearing patent letters; on return he was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 western Shu's Meng Zhixiang withheld tribute. The court sent Churang as credence envoy; on return he was Grand Master of Ceremonies by inspection.

sentences.zh: 應順初，授忻州刺史、檢校太保，充西北面都計度使，備北寇也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was appointed prefect of Xin, Grand Guardian by inspection, and overall frontier accountant of the northwest to guard against northern invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingshun he was Xin prefect, Grand Guardian by inspection, and northwest frontier accountant against northern raids.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年，入為左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he entered court as Left Valiant Guard general-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 2 he entered as Left Valiant Guard general-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，魏博屯將張令昭逐其帥以城叛，朝廷命範延光領兵討之，以處讓為河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year the Weibo garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao drove out his commander and rebelled with the city; the court ordered Fan Yanguang to lead troops against him and made Churang Hebei transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 3, summer, Weibo's Zhang Lingzhao rebelled. Fan Yanguang was sent against him with Churang as Hebei transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及高祖舉義於太原，處讓從至洛陽，乃授宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan, Churang followed to Luoyang and was appointed commissioner of the North Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Churang followed to Luoyang and became North Bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，轉左監門衛上將軍，充宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was transferred to Left Gate Guard general-in-chief and commissioner of the South Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 2 he was Left Gate Guard general-in-chief and South Bureau commissioner.

sentences.zh: 範延光之據鄴也，高祖命宣武軍節度使楊光遠領兵討之。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang held Ye, Gaozu ordered Xuanwu military governor Yang Guangyuan to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang held Ye, Gaozu sent Yang Guangyuan against him.

sentences.zh: 時處讓奉詔與光遠同參議軍政，會張從賓作亂於河陽，處讓自黎陽分兵討襲，從賓平，復與楊光遠同攻鄴城。

translations.literal: At the time Churang received orders to deliberate on military affairs with Guangyuan; when Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang, Churang divided troops from Liyang to strike; when Congbin was pacified he again with Yang Guangyuan jointly attacked Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Churang joined Guangyuan in planning. When Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang he split troops from Liyang to crush him, then rejoined the siege of Ye.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，範延光將謀納款，尚或遲留，處讓首入其城，以禍福諭之，延光乃降，以功加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year Fan Yanguang was about to offer surrender yet still hesitated; Churang was first to enter his city and lectured him on fortune and misfortune; Yanguang then surrendered; for merit he was given Grand Preceptor by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, winter, Fan Yanguang hesitated to surrender. Churang entered Ye first, lectured him on fortune and ruin, and Yanguang yielded. He was made Grand Preceptor by inspection.

sentences.zh: 先是，桑維翰、李崧兼充樞密使，處讓以莊宗已來，樞密使罕有宰臣兼者，因萌心以覬其位。

translations.literal: Earlier Sang Weihan and Li Song both also served as Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners; Churang because since Zhuangzong's time military affairs commissioners rarely also held chancellor posts, therefore conceived the ambition to covet that position.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan and Li Song had jointly held the Bureau of Military Affairs. Churang noted that since Zhuangzong few chancellors had doubled as commissioners, and he coveted the post.

sentences.zh: 及楊光遠討伐鄴城，軍機大事，高祖每命處讓宣達。

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan attacked Ye city, on great military affairs Gaozu each time ordered Churang to announce and convey them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guangyuan besieged Ye, Gaozu had Churang relay major military orders.

sentences.zh: 時光遠恃軍權，多有越體論奏，高祖依違而已，光遠慊之，頻與處讓宴語及之，處讓訴曰：「非聖旨也，皆出維翰等意。

translations.literal: At the time Guangyuan relied on military authority and often submitted memorials overstepping protocol; Gaozu was irresolute; Guangyuan resented this and frequently at banquets spoke with Churang about it; Churang complained: "It is not the holy edict—all comes from Weihan and the others."
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan abused his command and sent improper memorials. Gaozu wavered. Guangyuan complained to Churang at banquets; Churang said, "That is not the emperor—it is Weihan and the rest."

sentences.zh: 」及楊光遠入朝，遂於高祖前面言執政之失，高祖知其故，不得已乃罷維翰等，以處讓為樞密使。

translations.literal: " When Yang Guangyuan entered court he then before Gaozu spoke of the failures of those in power; Gaozu knew the reason and had no choice but to dismiss Weihan and the others and make Churang military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " When Guangyuan came to court he denounced the chancellors. Gaozu understood why and dismissed Weihan and others, making Churang military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時處讓每有敷奏，高祖多不稱旨，會處讓丁繼母憂，高祖因議罷樞密使，其本院庶事並委宰臣分判。

translations.literal: At the time whenever Churang had submissions Gaozu often found them not to his liking; when Churang entered mourning for his stepmother Gaozu therefore discussed abolishing the military affairs commissioner, and the routine business of that bureau was all entrusted to chancellors to divide and judge.
translations.idiomatic: Churang's advice often missed the mark. When he mourned his stepmother, Gaozu abolished the military affairs post and split its duties among chancellors.

sentences.zh: 處讓居喪期年，起復，授彰德軍節度使、澶衛等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: After Churang's mourning year he was recalled from mourning and appointed military governor of Zhangde Army and observation and disposition commissioner of Cao, Wei, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After a year of mourning he was recalled and made Zhangde military governor and observation commissioner of Cao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 子保勛，仕皇朝，位至省郎。

translations.literal: His son Baoqin served the imperial court and reached provincial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoqin served the dynasty as a provincial secretary.

sentences.zh: 李瓊，字隱光，滄州饒安人也。

translations.literal: Li Qiong, style Yinguang, was a native of Rao'an in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong, courtesy name Yinguang, was from Rao'an in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少籍本軍為騎士，莊宗平河朔，隸明宗麾下，漸升為小校。

translations.literal: In youth he was registered with his home army as a horseman; when Zhuangzong pacified Hebei he was attached to Mingzong's command and gradually rose to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served his home army as cavalry. After Zhuangzong took Hebei he joined Mingzong and rose to junior officer.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，明宗受詔，以本部兵送糧入薊門，時高祖從行，至涿州與敵相遇，高祖陷於圍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang Mingzong received orders to escort grain with his home troops into Jimen; at the time Gaozu followed on the march; at Zhuozhou they met the enemy and Gaozu was trapped in encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 2 Mingzong was ordered to escort grain to Jimen. Gaozu went along. At Zhuo they met the enemy and Gaozu was surrounded.

sentences.zh: 瓊顧諸軍已退，密牽高祖鐵衣，指東而遁。

translations.literal: Qiong saw the armies had already withdrawn and secretly pulled Gaozu's iron armor, pointing east to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the army had withdrawn, Qiong tugged Gaozu's armor and led him east.

sentences.zh: 至劉李河，為敵所襲，瓊浮水先至南岸，高祖至河中，馬倒，順流而下，瓊以所執長矛援高祖出之，又以所跨馬奉高祖，瓊徒步護之，奔十餘里，乃入涿州。

translations.literal: At Liu-Li River they were struck by the enemy; Qiong swam and first reached the south bank; Gaozu reached mid-river, his horse fell, and he drifted downstream; Qiong with the long spear he held helped Gaozu out, then gave Gaozu the horse he rode; Qiong on foot protected him and ran more than ten li before entering Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu-Li River they were attacked. Qiong swam to the south bank first. Gaozu's horse fell mid-river; Qiong pulled him out with his spear, gave him his horse, and ran on foot beside him ten li into Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 高祖薦於明宗，明宗賞之，尋超授軍職。

translations.literal: Gaozu recommended him to Mingzong; Mingzong rewarded him and soon gave him extraordinary military rank.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu recommended him to Mingzong, who rewarded him and soon promoted him.

sentences.zh: 同光末，明宗討趙在禮於鄴。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang Mingzong attacked Zhao Zaili at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tongguang Mingzong attacked Zhao Zaili at Ye.

sentences.zh: 鄴軍既變，明宗退至魏縣，遣高祖以騎士三百疾趨汴州。

translations.literal: When the Ye army mutinied Mingzong withdrew to Wei County and sent Gaozu with three hundred horsemen to hurry to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Ye army mutinied. Mingzong fell back to Wei County and sent Gaozu with three hundred horsemen to Bian.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗遣騎將西方鄴守其城，高祖憂之，使瓊以勁兵突封丘門而入，高祖踵之，鄴尋歸命，浚郊遂定。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuangzong sent the horse general Xifang Ye to guard the city; Gaozu was worried and had Qiong with picked troops burst through the Fengqiu gate and enter; Gaozu followed on his heels; Ye soon submitted and the outskirts were secured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent Xifang Ye to hold the city. Gaozu sent Qiong to burst through Fengqiu Gate; Ye soon submitted and the capital was secured.

sentences.zh: 及高祖領陜州，奏補雲騎指揮使，俄改侍衛牙隊指揮使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took Shaanzhou he memorialized to appoint him commander of the Cloud Horse Guard; soon he was changed to commander of the palace guard tooth unit.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu governed Shaan he made him Cloud Horse commander, then palace guard tooth-unit commander.

sentences.zh: 長興中，從高祖討東川，至劍州，使瓊以部下兵破賊軍數千，身中重創，軍還，改龍武指揮使。

translations.literal: In Changxing he followed Gaozu against eastern Shu; reaching Jianzhou he had Qiong with his troops break several thousand bandit troops; he took heavy wounds; when the army returned he was changed to Dragon Martial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing he followed Gaozu against eastern Shu. At Jian, Qiong routed thousands of rebels and took grave wounds. On return he became Dragon Martial commander.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，屯雲州，累擒獲契丹人馬，以功改右捧聖軍指揮使。

translations.literal: In Qingtai he garrisoned Yunzhou and repeatedly captured Khitan men and horses; by merit he was changed to commander of the Right Supporting Sage Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qingtai he garrisoned Yun, repeatedly captured Khitan troops and horses, and became Right Supporting Sage commander.

sentences.zh: 唐末帝以瓊元事高祖，乃自塞下移授單州馬步軍副指揮使。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Tang because Qiong had long served Gaozu moved him from the frontier down to appoint deputy commander of Shanzhou horse and foot army.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor moved him from the frontier to deputy commander of Shan's horse and foot army because he had long served Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，補護聖都指揮使，又念疇昔輟馬導護之力，前後所賜金帛甚厚，但未升爵位，瓊亦郁郁然。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he supplemented him as Protecting Sage commander; he also remembered the strength of giving up his horse and guiding protection in former days; before and after the gifts of gold and silk were very thick, yet he was not advanced in noble rank, and Qiong was also depressed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made him Protecting Sage commander and heaped gold and silk on him for the old rescue, but gave no noble rank—and Qiong brooded.

sentences.zh: 久之，領橫州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he led Hengzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he became Heng prefect.

sentences.zh: 五年，出典申州，微有政聲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out to govern Shenzhou and had slight reputation in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he governed Shen and earned a modest reputation.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，入為殿前散員都指揮使，遙領雷州，俄遷棣州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded he entered court as commander of all scattered attendants before the throne, held Leizhou in absentia, and soon was moved to Di prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded he became commander of throne attendants, held Lei in absentia, then became Di prefect.

sentences.zh: 遇楊光遠以青州叛，自統本部兵攻其城，且以書誘瓊，瓊因拒之，以書上進，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled with Qingzhou he himself commanded his home troops to attack the city and also sent letters to entice Qiong; Qiong therefore refused him and forwarded the letters upward; the court praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled at Qing, Qiong refused his letters and reported them—the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，改洺州團練使，累官至加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he was changed to regimental commissioner of Mo and rose by stages to Minister of Works by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 2 he was Mo regimental commissioner and rose to Minister of Works by inspection.

sentences.zh: 三年，授護聖右廂都指揮使，領岳州團練使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed commander of the Right Wing of the Protecting Sage and regimental commissioner of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was Right Protecting Sage wing commander and Yue regimental commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時洺州吏民列狀保留，朝廷不允。

translations.literal: At the time Mozhou officials and people filed petitions to retain him; the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhou petitioned to keep him; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 及杜重威降敵，改授瓊威州刺史。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei surrendered to the enemy he was changed and appointed Wei prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei surrendered to the enemy, Qiong was made Wei prefect.

sentences.zh: 行及鄭州，遇群盜攻郡，與方太禦賊，中流矢而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: On the march reaching Zhengzhou he met bandits attacking the prefecture; with Fang Tai he repelled the bandits and died of a wound from a flying arrow at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Zheng he met bandits attacking the city. With Fang Tai he fought them off but died of an arrow wound at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 高漢筠，字時英，齊州歷山人也。

translations.literal: Gao Hanjun, style Shiying, was a native of Lishan in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hanjun, courtesy name Shiying, was from Lishan in Qi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖詣，嘗為是邑令，故家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi had once been magistrate of this district, hence the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi had been magistrate of the district, so the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 漢筠少好書傳，嘗詣長白山講肄，會唐末齊、魯交兵，梁氏方霸，乃擲筆謁焉，尋納於軍門。

translations.literal: Hanjun in youth loved books and classics; he once went to Changbai Mountain to lecture and study; when at the end of Tang Qi and Lu were at war and the Liang clan was just dominating, he threw down his brush and went to pay court, soon being enrolled at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hanjun loved learning and studied on Changbai Mountain. When Qi and Lu warred at the end of Tang he joined Liang's army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為衛州牙校。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as junior officer of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was a Weizhou junior officer.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，莊宗入魏，分兵諭其屬郡，時漢筠以利病說衛之牧守，俾送款於莊宗，以漢筠為功，尋移洺州都校。

translations.literal: In Tianyou of Tang Zhuangzong entered Wei and divided troops to announce to subordinate prefectures; at the time Hanjun with advantage and harm persuaded Wei's governor to send submission to Zhuangzong; taking Hanjun as meritorious, soon he was moved to chief officer of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Tianyou Zhuangzong entered Wei. Hanjun persuaded Wei's governor to submit and was moved to chief officer of Mo.

sentences.zh: 其後改常山為北京，以漢筠為皇城使，加檢校兵部尚書、左驍衛將軍同正。

translations.literal: Afterward Changshan was changed to the Northern Capital and Hanjun was made imperial city commissioner, given Minister of War by inspection and Left Valiant Guard general with full rank.
translations.idiomatic: Changshan became the Northern Capital; Hanjun was imperial city commissioner, Minister of War by inspection, and Left Valiant Guard general.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，除成德軍節度副使，俄以荊門用軍，促詔漢筠移倅襄州，權知軍州事。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was made deputy military governor of Chengde Army; soon because Jingmen needed troops an urgent edict moved Hanjun to deputy at Xiangzhou with acting authority over military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong made him Chengde deputy military governor, then acting Xiangzhou administrator when Jingmen needed troops.

sentences.zh: 長興中，歷曹、亳二州刺史。

translations.literal: In Changxing he served in succession as prefect of Cao and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing he was Cao and Bo prefect in turn.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，加檢校司徒，行左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was given Grand Master of Ceremonies by inspection and acted as Left Golden Spear Guard general-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was Grand Master of Ceremonies by inspection and acting Left Golden Spear general-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，高祖建義於河東，唐末帝遣晉昌節度使張敬達率師圍太原，委漢筠巡撫其郡。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai Gaozu raised the righteous cause in Hedong; the Last Emperor of Tang sent Jinchang military governor Zhang Jingda to lead troops to besiege Taiyuan and entrusted Hanjun to pacify the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai Gaozu rose in Hedong. The Last Emperor sent Zhang Jingda to besiege Taiyuan and left Hanjun to pacify the city.

sentences.zh: 及敬達遇害，節度副使田承肇率部兵攻漢筠於府署，漢筠乃啟關延承肇，謂曰：「仆與子俱承朝寄，而相迫何甚？

translations.literal: When Jingda met disaster the deputy military governor Tian Chengzhao led headquarters troops to attack Hanjun at the government offices; Hanjun then opened the gate and admitted Chengzhao and said: "I and you both bear the court's commission—why press so hard?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jingda was killed, deputy Tian Chengzhao attacked Hanjun at headquarters. Hanjun opened the gate and said, "We both serve the court—why press so hard?"

sentences.zh: 」承肇曰：「我欲扶公為節度使。

translations.literal: " Chengzhao said: "I wish to support you as military governor."
translations.idiomatic: " Chengzhao said, "I want to make you military governor."

sentences.zh: 」澤筠曰：「老夫耄矣，不敢首為亂階，死生系子籌之。

translations.literal: " Hanjun said: "This old man is aged; I dare not be first to make a step of disorder—life and death depend on your planning."
translations.idiomatic: " Hanjun said, "I am old and will not start a rebellion—my life is in your hands."

sentences.zh: 」承肇目左右令前，諸軍投刃於地，曰：「高金吾累朝宿德，不可枉殺。

translations.literal: " Chengzhao signaled those beside him to advance; the troops cast blades to the ground and said: "High Golden Spear has virtue over many reigns—he cannot be wrongly killed."
translations.idiomatic: " Chengzhao signaled his men forward; they threw down their weapons and said, "Lord Gao is too venerable to kill."

sentences.zh: 」承肇以眾意難拒，遂謝云：「與公戲耳！

translations.literal: " Chengzhao because the host's will was hard to refuse then apologized: "I was jesting with you!"
translations.idiomatic: " Chengzhao apologized, "Only a jest!"

sentences.zh: 」漢筠促騎以還。

translations.literal: " Hanjun urged his horse to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Hanjun rode back.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，飛詔征之，遇諸途，乃入覲，尋遷左驍衛大將軍、內客省使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he sent a flying edict summoning him; meeting on the road he then entered audience and soon was moved to Left Valiant Guard general-in-chief and commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu entered Luoyang and summoned him by express. He met Gaozu on the road, attended court, and became Left Valiant Guard general-in-chief and Inner Reception commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天福三年正月，遘疾，終東京之私第，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Tianfu he met illness and died at his private residence in the eastern capital at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 3, month 1, he fell ill and died at his home in the eastern capital at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 漢筠性寬厚，儀容偉如也。

translations.literal: Hanjun was generous by nature and his bearing was imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjun was generous and imposing in bearing.

sentences.zh: 雖歷戎職，未嘗有非法之言出於口吻，多慕士大夫所為，復以清白自負。

translations.literal: Though he held military posts, never did unlawful words come from his lips; he much admired what scholar-officials did and also took purity as his pride.
translations.idiomatic: Though a soldier, he spoke no impropriety, admired scholars, and prized integrity.

sentences.zh: 在襄陽，有孽吏常課外獻白金二十鎰，漢筠曰：「非多納枿泬，則刻削阛鋏，吾有正俸，此何用焉！
