translations.literal: At Xiangyang a corrupt clerk regularly levied extra tribute of twenty ingots of white gold; Hanjun said: "If you do not over-collect bribes, you will carve down the market stalls—I have regular salary—what use is this!"
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang a corrupt clerk offered twenty ingots of extra silver. Hanjun said, "I have my salary—what need of this?"

sentences.zh: 」因戒其主者不復然，其白金皆以狀上進，有詔嘉之。

translations.literal: " He therefore warned his chief not to do so again; the white gold was all submitted upward by memorial; there was an edict praising this.
translations.idiomatic: " He forbade it and sent all the silver to court with a memorial; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 及蒞濟陰，部民安之，四邑飯僧凡有萬八千人。

translations.literal: When he arrived at Jiyin the people of the circuit were secure; in four districts he fed monks totaling eighteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiyin the people were at peace; he fed eighteen thousand monks in four districts.

sentences.zh: 在亳州三年，歲以己俸百千代納逋租，斯亦近代之良二千石也。

translations.literal: In Bozhou for three years each year with his own salary of a hundred strings he paid overdue rent on others' behalf—this too is a good two-thousand-dan official of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: At Bo for three years he paid others' overdue rents from his salary—a model prefect of his age.

sentences.zh: 長子貞文，仕皇朝，為開封少尹，卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhenwen served the imperial court as vice magistrate of Kaifeng and died.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhenwen served as Kaifeng vice magistrate and died.

sentences.zh: 彥韜出於軍旅，植性和厚，理綿州日，甚著綏懷之譽，故有賞典旌焉。

translations.literal: Yantao came from the military camps; his nature was harmonious and thick; in governing Mianzhou he was very renowned for soothing and cherishing, hence there was reward and commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Yantao came from the army, was good-natured, and won fame soothing Mian—hence court rewards.

sentences.zh: 在濮陽，屬清泰末，群寇入郡，郡人大擾，彥韜率帳下百人，一呼破之，人皆感之。

translations.literal: At Puyang, belonging to the end of Qingtai, when bandits entered the prefecture and the people were greatly disturbed, Yantao led a hundred men of his headquarters; one shout broke them and people were all grateful.
translations.idiomatic: At Puyang late in Qingtai, when bandits raided the prefecture he routed them with a hundred men at one shout.

sentences.zh: 但不能守廉養正，以終令譽。

translations.literal: But he could not guard integrity and cultivate rectitude to the end of a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He could not keep his integrity to the end.

sentences.zh: 長興中，罷密州赴闕，苞苴甚厚。

translations.literal: In Changxing he left Mizhou for court with gifts very thick.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing he left Mi for court laden with gifts.

sentences.zh: 起甲第於洛陽，逾月而成，華堂廣廡，亞王公之家，見者嗤之。

translations.literal: He built a grand mansion in Luoyang completed in a month; splendid halls and broad galleries rivaled princes' houses—those who saw it mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: He built a Luoyang mansion in a month grand as a prince's house—and was mocked for it.

sentences.zh: 故淹翔五郡，位不及廉察，抑有由也。

translations.literal: Therefore he lingered through five prefectures yet his rank never reached inspector—there was reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: He held five posts but never rose to inspector—for good reason.

sentences.zh: 李彥珣，邢州人也。

translations.literal: Li Yanxun was a native of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanxun was from Xing.

sentences.zh: 少為郡之牙吏。

translations.literal: In youth he was a junior clerk of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was a prefectural clerk.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，明宗鎮其地，彥珣素無檢節，因洽於左右，明宗即位，以為通事舍人。

translations.literal: In Tianyou of Tang Mingzong governed the place; Yanxun by nature had no restraint and through contact with those beside Mingzong, when Mingzong took the throne he was made Grand Secretariat courier.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong governed Xing in Tang Tianyou, the unrestrained Yanxun curried favor and became Grand Secretariat courier when Mingzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣使東川，行至其境，其仆從為董璋所收，彥珣竄還，以失敬故也。

translations.literal: He was once sent as envoy to eastern Shu; reaching its border his attendants were seized by Dong Zhang; Yanxun fled back—for lack of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to eastern Shu, his attendants were seized by Dong Zhang and he fled home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 朝廷攻璋，詔授行營步軍都監。

translations.literal: When the court attacked Zhang an edict appointed him campaign foot army superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: When the court attacked Zhang he was made campaign foot army superintendent.

sentences.zh: 彥珣素不孝於父母，在鄉絕其供饋，同列惡其鄙惡，旋出為外任。

translations.literal: Yanxun was by nature unfilial toward parents; in his home district he cut off their provisions; colleagues hated his baseness and soon he went out to external appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He starved his parents and colleagues despised him; he was soon sent to posts outside court.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，遷河陽行軍司馬，遇張從賓為亂，因朋助之，從賓敗，奔於魏州。

translations.literal: In Qingtai he was moved to Heyang campaign secretary; when Zhang Congbin rebelled he joined him as a confederate; when Congbin was defeated he fled to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qingtai he was Heyang campaign secretary, aided Zhang Congbin's revolt, and fled to Wei when Congbin fell.

sentences.zh: 範延光既叛，署為步軍都監，委以守陴。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang had rebelled he was appointed foot army superintendent and entrusted with guarding the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang rebelled he was made foot army superintendent and entrusted with the walls.

sentences.zh: 招討使楊光遠以彥珣見用，欲撓延光而誘彥珣，乃遣人就邢臺訪得其母，令於城下以招之。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Yang Guangyuan because Yanxun was employed wished to shake Yanguang and entice Yanxun; he therefore sent someone to Xing platform to find his mother and had her at the foot of the wall summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan, to undermine Fan Yanguang, found Yanxun's mother at Xing and had her call to him from below the wall.

sentences.zh: 彥珣識其母，發矢以斃之，見者傷之。

translations.literal: Yanxun recognized his mother and shot an arrow to kill her; those who saw were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxun recognized her and shot her dead—to the horror of onlookers.

sentences.zh: 及隨延光出降，授坊州刺史。

translations.literal: When he followed Yanguang out to surrender he was appointed Fang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan surrendered, Yanxun was made Fang prefect.

sentences.zh: 近臣以彥珣之惡逆奏於高祖，高祖曰：「赦命已行，不可改也。

translations.literal: Close ministers memorialized Yanxun's wicked rebellion to Gaozu; Gaozu said: "The amnesty edict has already been issued—it cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers denounced Yanxun to Gaozu, who said, "The amnesty is already issued and cannot be revoked."

sentences.zh: 」遂令赴郡，後不知其所終焉。

translations.literal: " He then ordered him to go to his prefecture; later his end is not known.
translations.idiomatic: " He was ordered to his post; his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》云：彥珣後以坐贓誅。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang's History says: Yanxun was later executed for corruption.)
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang's History says: Yanxun was later executed for corruption.)

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔從簡從莊宗戰於河上，可謂勇矣，及其為末帝守於孟津，豈得為忠乎？

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In former days Congjian fought with Zhuangzong on the river—one may call that brave; yet when he held Mengjin for the Last Emperor, could one call that loyal?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Congjian was brave on the river under Zhuangzong, but holding Mengjin for the Last Emperor was not loyalty.

sentences.zh: 忠既無聞，勇何足貴！

translations.literal: Loyalty was unheard of—what is bravery worth!
translations.idiomatic: Without loyalty, what is bravery worth?

sentences.zh: 潘環、方太，雖鹹負雄幹，而俱歿亂世，蓋方略不足以衛其身故也。

translations.literal: Pan Huan and Fang Tai, though they all bore heroic frames, yet both perished in chaotic times—probably their stratagems were insufficient to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Huan and Fang Tai were strong men but died in chaos—their strategy could not save them.

sentences.zh: 何建舉秦、隴之封，附巴、邛之俗，守方之寄，其若是乎！

translations.literal: He Jian raised the seals of Qin and Long and attached to Ba and Qiong customs—the trust of guarding a region, was it like this!
translations.idiomatic: He Jian took Qin and Long and went over to Ba and Qiong ways—is that how a frontier guardian should act?

sentences.zh: 其餘皆儋珪析爵之流也，亦可以垂名於是矣。

translations.literal: The rest were all of the stream of Tan Gui who split noble ranks—they too could leave names here.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were men who traded rank for favor, yet names remain.

sentences.zh: 秘瓊既覆董氏之族，旋為鄴帥所屠，何報應之速也！

translations.literal: Mi Qiong having overthrown the Dong clan was in turn butchered by the Ye commander—how swift the retribution!
translations.idiomatic: Mi Qiong destroyed the Dong clan and was slaughtered by the Ye commander—swift retribution!

sentences.zh: 惟彥珣忍射其親，殆非人類，晉祖宥之不戮，蓋失刑之甚也。

translations.literal: Only Yanxun could bear to shoot his kin—hardly human; the Jin founder spared him from execution—probably a grave failure of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanxun shot his own mother—barely human. That Gaozu spared him was a grave failure of justice.
